title: Volume 1 Chapter 4: Experimental Machine
content: A few days had passed since the attack. The academy was closed for the day since it was Sunday, and I was on standby in the hangar lent to the Prometheus Project's development team since morning.

"Alright, alright!"  
"Hurry up and remove the fixtures!"  
"Make sure to check the contents of the container thoroughly!"

The maintenance crew was bustling about, busy from the morning. In the hangar, preparations were underway for the arrival of the experimental machine, which was central to the project. I stood in a corner, trying not to be in the way, gazing at the experimental machine that had its coverings removed and was now standing inside the hangar.
"This is my first time seeing a humanoid weapon in person," I muttered.

The humanoid weapon, developed with high expectations for combat against Gijuu, had proven ineffective on the battlefield, leading to the cancellation of the development project itself. The development team had recovered the stored unit, performed maintenance and modifications, and brought it to the Third Academy.
Alison Green was nearby, occasionally glancing at the busy maintenance crew while sitting on a folding chair she had brought out. She was operating a tablet, checking the future plans.

"It's been over ten years since the project was canceled, hasn't it? The experimental machine we brought seems to be one that was sleeping in some warehouse. It looks like the maintenance was quite a task," she said, her gaze still fixed on the tablet screen.
"Can a machine that’s over ten years old still operate?"

"I made it operational. After all, the Prometheus Project has no significant achievements to show for itself. There are limits to the budget the organization can provide. We have to use whatever we can."
"Is that what they call being pragmatic?"
From my perspective, anything usable should be utilized, but the lack of resources to develop new units for the project seemed to reflect the current state of the development team.
"I never thought I'd hear you say something so pragmatic," Alison remarked, looking up with interest, which reminded me of a man who often complained.

"A foul-mouthed colleague used to say that often."  
"Oh, really?"
Alison lost interest in my story and turned her gaze back to the experimental machine. The machine, now free from its fixtures, looked heavy with its thick armor.
As I was watching, a particularly energetic mushroom-headed scientist entered the hangar. It was Dr. Smith.

"Ichinose-kun, how have you been? I was surprised to hear you were transferred to Class Five, but it seems like you’re doing well being here. Still, I’m amazed by the principal of the Third Academy's thinking. I thought they would keep their distance, but who would have thought they’d let you interact with the Valkyries? The principal who accepted our development team is quite the eccentric."
Having finished his greeting and his thoughts, Dr. Smith seemed satisfied and approached Alison before I could respond.
"It’s good to see you well, Alison. By the way, could you listen to me? I had a new idea while maintaining the experimental machine—"
He began to ramble on to Alison, who seemed to have known him for a long time. Not wanting to hear a long story, she quickly responded.
"Yes, I’m doing well. Let’s save the discussion about the experimental machine for later. Now that we have both the pilot and the machine, I’d like to discuss the future plans."
Alison seemed to know how to handle Dr. Smith. Although he was cut off, he didn’t seem to mind at all.
"Right. For now, let’s start with the activation test of the experimental machine."
Hearing about the activation test of the humanoid weapon, I decided to ask a question that had been on my mind.

"Dr. Smith, may I ask a question?"  
"What is it, Ichinose-kun?"  
"I’ve heard that the experimental machine was maintained on the ground. Couldn’t the activation test have been done there as well?"  
"Ah, of course. It operated without any issues on the ground. However, that was only if a regular pilot operated it. If you were to pilot a machine equipped with a Magic Power Converter, I can’t guarantee that no anomalies would occur. After all, experiments involving magic should be conducted at the academy. You see, it’s a matter of confidentiality."
It seemed that the devices installed could potentially cause issues, so conducting the experiment was necessary. Alison appeared to be in agreement with the activation test.

"Originally, you’re an infantryman, not a pilot. We plan to conduct training with the actual machine alongside the activation test."  
"Thank you for answering my question."

As I saluted, Dr. Smith chuckled.  
"You’re still the same, Ichinose-kun. With that attitude, you might stand out in this academy."  
"Yes, I’m aware that I stand out."
Just being a boy in a girls' school classroom made me stand out, but it seemed my personality was also quite different from that of a typical male student. I was aware that I stood out in Class Five.

Alison let out a deep sigh at my response.  
"What an energetic reply."  
"Thank you."  
"It was sarcasm. You should study common sense along with Dr. Smith."

As I was told to learn common sense by Alison, Dr. Smith, who had thought he was unrelated to the conversation, was surprised to hear his name mentioned.  
"Wait, me too?"

Having changed into my pilot suit, I slipped into the cramped cockpit of the experimental machine. It was already a struggle to move in there, but with the additional experimental instruments, it felt even more cramped.

I sat in the pilot seat, fastened my seatbelt, and began the preparations to activate the machine.  
"This is test pilot Ichinose Ren, commencing the activation of the prototype experimental machine XFA–10 Thunderbolt modified version."
As I communicated this to the development team through the intercom, Dr. Smith’s face appeared on the activated monitor.

There didn’t seem to be any problems, but he had something on his mind.  
"Hmm, you’re too stiff. Let’s take it easy, Ichinose-kun."  
"Take it easy, you say? Even if you tell me that, I—"

As I replied, which was often said to lack excitement, Dr. Smith raised his palm towards me, signaling me to shut my mouth. Understanding this, I fell silent. After pondering for a moment, Dr. Smith smiled and nodded several times.

"You can call the machine Thunderbolt. Even though it’s a modified version, it was never officially adopted as an experimental machine. The real issue is your call sign, Ichinose-kun. In situations like this, pilots are usually called by their call signs, right?"  
"A call sign, you say? ...When I was in the infantry, I was called Cherry."

As I mentioned my nostalgic call sign, an inexplicable tightness gripped my chest. On the other side of the monitor, Dr. Smith tilted his head.  
"You were called Cherry? Cherry, huh? That doesn’t quite match your image. Is there a reason behind it?"  
"That’s because I—"

As I tried to explain the meaning, Alison deliberately cleared her throat loudly, interrupting the conversation.  
"Let’s change your call sign to something new. Do you have any preferences, Lieutenant?"  
"No, I have an attachment to Cherry."  
"Does Dr. Smith have any suggestions?"

It seemed that Alison didn’t expect that answer and sought Dr. Smith’s opinion on the call sign.  
"I-Fazft... that might be a bit hard to say, huh? Then let’s go with Envy. Yes, from today on, Ichinose-kun’s call sign will be Envy."

Dr. Smith wore a satisfied expression, while Alison looked exasperated.  
"You’ve put quite a bit of sarcasm into that, Dr. Smith. Is this a criticism of the higher-ups?"

Since criticizing the higher-ups was a serious matter, I couldn’t remain silent.  
"I believe that critical remarks are not advisable."

Worried, Dr. Smith adjusted his glasses with his middle finger while smiling.  
"I-Fazft means jealousy in Japanese. Envy has the same meaning. It’s a fitting call sign for us, who are envious of the Valkyries’ power. Don’t you think?"  
"Envy, huh..."

What kind of call sign is that? While I thought that, memories of being called Cherry in my previous squad resurfaced. In the old military, it seemed they sometimes deliberately assigned strange call signs. After the Gijuu invasion, the Fairy Agency restructured the collapsed military. Even after the restructuring, the military’s customs remained and have been passed down to the present day.

Being called Cherry and now being referred to as Envy felt oddly familiar. If I changed from Cherry to Envy, my former squadmates would have teased me, saying it was "too cool."  
"I... agree. Call sign Envy, understood."

As I agreed with Dr. Smith's suggestion, Alison furrowed her brow.  
"I never thought you would agree. ...I’ll really register you as Envy. Don’t come complaining to me later."  
"Don’t worry. In fact, I think the Valkyries will be pleased. After all, we’re just borrowing their space. Let’s show them a humble attitude."
By calling myself Envy and trying to curry favor with the female students of the Third Academy, it felt like it reflected the current state of our development team.
The activation of the Thunderbolt proceeded without any issues. The activation test had already been completed, and it was determined that the machine operated normally before being transported.

Now piloting the activated Thunderbolt, I was walking in a square prepared near the hangar. Although it was called a square, it was just a place piled with containers, and the usable space was limited. When the development team pleaded for an experimental area, the academy designated this area, which was not well organized.
They told us to clean it up ourselves if we wanted to secure an experimental area. Currently, I was maneuvering the Thunderbolt along a course set up with containers arranged as obstacles.
"I have reached the destination."

After successfully walking the machine to the goal point, the development team lightly applauded. Along with the sound of applause coming through the communication device, I heard Alison’s voice.  
"It seems there are no issues. I’d like to complete most of the check items today, so please wait in the cockpit until the next test preparations are finished."  
"Understood."

Ordered to wait in the cramped cockpit, I checked the functions to get accustomed to piloting as quickly as possible.  
"The control stick is stiffer than the simulator. The pedals could be a bit heavier."

While summarizing the necessary information for the next adjustments when I returned, I enlarged the monitor’s display. I switched to thermal imaging and various screens, trying to memorize the controls.

As I checked each one, I realized just how expensive a humanoid weapon was.  
"This is completely different from the suit I used as an infantryman. With this kind of performance..."

Had the mortality rate in ground combat significantly decreased? As I pondered this, I shook my head, realizing that the cost wouldn’t balance out.  
"...It’s no use thinking about it now. Still, despite having this much armor, it seems ineffective against Gijuu class 2 and above."

When the humanoid weapon was developed, it seemed that most units were of the heavy armor type. The conclusion was that thick armor was essential to withstand attacks from Gijuu class 2 and above. However, such thick armor was apparently meaningless in front of the Gijuu.

The theory that armor without a force field was ineffective in battles against Gijuu had only been reinforced. Furthermore, if the force field couldn’t be used for attacks, it wouldn’t deal effective damage to the Gijuu. The humanoid weapon had merely ended up being a large target for the enemy.
"...If the machine is equipped with a Magic Power Converter, this problem could be solved."

In the Prometheus Project, the humanoid weapon, which had ended up being a large target, was equipped with a Magic Power Converter. The reason for equipping it to the humanoid weapon was that the converter was too large to be carried by infantry.

There were proposals to mount it on tanks or fighter jets, but it seemed they ultimately settled on repurposing the humanoid weapon, which had failed despite the enormous budget invested. According to Dr. Smith, "Humanoids are more efficient," but the details surrounding this were classified, and as a test pilot, I was not informed.

However, there was no doubt that being a humanoid weapon had its significance.  
"Hmm?"

As I moved the machine's camera eye, I noticed a group of female students watching from a distance. There were about six of them, and among them was a distinctive girl. It was clear from the monitor that the other girls were being considerate towards her.

The girl with red hair fluttering in the wind was wearing a distinctive cape.  
"A red cape... that must be Hayase-san."

I had never seen any other female students wearing a red cape at the academy, so I was sure of it. As I muttered to myself in the cockpit, Hayase-san seemed to notice my gaze, furrowing her brows in displeasure before turning her back and walking away.

It looked like she said a word or two to the surrounding girls before they also began to leave.  
"Did she notice my gaze from this distance? ...No way."

As I muttered to myself, Dr. Smith, perhaps curious about my mumbling, spoke up.  
"Talking to yourself?"  
"Sorry. I noticed that the female students from the academy were watching the experiment."  
"Ah, that’s not good. This is supposed to be a top-secret experiment, so it would be troublesome if they saw it."  
"Should we inform the academy?"  
"Well, we’re just borrowing their space. The academy might protect the girls, I suppose. By the way, what kind of girls were watching?"  
"The most distinctive one was Hayase-san... the girl wearing the red cape."

As I shared Hayase-san's characteristics, Alison interrupted the conversation.  
"That’s the ace. Even if you protest to the academy, I doubt there will be any significant punishment."  
"Ace?"  
"There are four colors of capes: blue, green, yellow... and red. Only the top ace of each class is allowed to wear them. The ace is an important asset to the academy, so they’ll probably just get a warning."  
"Hayase-san is the academy's ace... well, I suppose that makes sense."

She was capable and exuded confidence. Louise had also highly praised her abilities, so there was no doubt about it. However, like the other female students, she had a stern expression, seemingly opposed to the Prometheus Project. The disdain in her gaze directed at the Thunderbolt was palpable.

The next day.  
In Class Five, I was talking with Louise during break time. The topic was yesterday's incident.  
"Hayase-san, Hayase Maya, is definitely the ace of Boots Cat."

Confused by the unfamiliar term, I repeated Louise's words.  
"Boots Cat? Is that her call sign?"  
Louise shook her head and explained patiently, incorporating details about the academy's circumstances.  
"Classes One to Four have specific colors and names. For example, Class One is blue and called Bluebird. Class Three is red and called Boots Cat."  
"Is that the name of the unit?"

I rested my chin on my hand, trying to understand, and it seemed I was correct, as Louise nodded.  
"Exactly. Normally, it’s just the class name, but on the battlefield, it’s used as the unit name. And only Hayase-san is allowed to wear the red cape. So if there was a girl wearing a red cape there, it’s definitely her."  
"I’ve heard that colored capes are a sign of being an ace... But why was she there? I can’t believe an ace would ignore orders from the base command."  
"I don’t know either."

Alison had mentioned that the Prometheus Project was a bundle of secrets, and the academy had issued a notice to avoid approaching it carelessly. If she was an ace at the academy, she would likely be in a representative position among the female students. The rules and customs were too different from a normal base, so I could only speculate, but it was clear she held a prominent position.
Hayase Maya— I didn’t want to believe that she was the kind of person who would ignore orders. As I was pondering, three female students approached us. Their expressions didn’t seem friendly.

They ignored Louise and directed their conversation towards me. Slamming their hands on the desk, they confronted me with an intimidating attitude.  
"I heard you regenerated your lost limbs with Gijuu cells?"

If I had let my guard down, I might have reacted to her words in shock. I forced myself to maintain a blank expression. The thought that crossed my mind was, "How did they find out?" The regenerative surgery using Gijuu cells was classified information within the Prometheus Project.

It wasn’t something that could be easily noticed, like the Thunderbolt. Suddenly, I recalled the attackers who had called themselves fallen angels. Where had the information leaked from? Had they leaked it? Thoughts raced through my mind that I needed to inform the doctors immediately.
"...I don’t understand the intent behind your question."

I tried to deflect the situation and quickly contact the doctors, but the girls wouldn’t let me escape. I noticed that the mention of Gijuu had caused the surrounding female students to react, and the once noisy classroom fell silent.

They were all glaring at me with piercing gazes.  
"Don’t play dumb. The information is already out. You regenerated your lost limbs using Gijuu cells, didn’t you?"

How much information had leaked? Feeling anxious, I tried to maintain my composure while thinking of a way to navigate this situation. When I glanced at the clock in the classroom, I saw that the instructor would arrive in just a few minutes.

I could wait, but this was an emergency. I should ignore the class and join the development team to discuss what to do next. As I tried to stand up, I realized that the other female students had moved to block my escape route.

A few of them stood at the entrance of the classroom, while the rest surrounded me. All their eyes were filled with hostility. The girl who had questioned me wore a fierce expression.  
"I found it strange how a man who can’t use magic could fight against Gijuu. I never expected you to attach limbs using Gijuu cells."

To the female students who had undergone rigorous training to fight against Gijuu, it seemed I was not much different from the Gijuu themselves. The conversation also touched on the incident from a few days ago when we were attacked.  
"I heard you used Gijuu’s power when you were attacked?"  
"!?!"

I nearly let out a sound, clenching my hands tightly to hold back. I hadn’t expected information from just a few days ago to have leaked.  
"Stop being silent and say something. Or do you want to be taken down right here?"

Perhaps they had procured knives before coming here, as the girls had hidden them under their cardigans. As I considered how to force my way out of this situation, Louise stepped forward, spreading her arms to shield me from the girls.  
"Everyone, that’s enough! The teacher is about to arrive!"

As Louise raised her voice, the instructor entered the classroom. He seemed to have noticed the tense atmosphere and crossed his arms, observing the situation. However, he didn’t intervene.  
"You all have been quite noisy. Honestly, the whims of the principal are troublesome. Just to let you know, don’t cause too much of a ruckus."

Although his attitude was passive, the instructor glared at the girls who had brought weapons into the classroom.  
"If you cause a disturbance, it wouldn’t be surprising if the talk of scouts and recommendations disappeared. If you don’t want to graduate from Class Five, you better restrain yourselves."

At the instructor’s words, all the female students instantly tensed up. The words scout, recommendation... and graduation made them react sensitively. As I silently tried to leave the classroom, Louise urged me to sit down.  
"Stay for now; I want to talk later."  
"But I have a duty to inform the development team about this situation."  
"If that’s the case... what if I said I have a lead on who leaked the information?"

I was slightly surprised by Louise’s claim that she had an idea about the source of the information leak.  
"You know something?"

Louise nodded seriously.  
"The next break will be lunchtime. Let’s talk then."  
"...Understood."
Desperate for clues, I decided to message Alison to inform her that classified information had leaked before attending the class.

When lunchtime arrived, Louise led me to the rooftop of the school building.  
"Isn’t this a restricted area? There was a sign along the way."

Standing near the fence on the rooftop, Louise explained her reason for choosing this spot.  
"I’m sorry. But no one comes here."  
"You don’t want anyone to overhear."

From Louise's actions, it seemed that providing me with information had its drawbacks for her as well. Knowing the risks, Louise was willing to share information with me, but it wasn’t guaranteed to be accurate. There was no evidence, but she seemed to believe it was almost certain.

"I don’t have confirmation, but I thought of one point after hearing your story."  
"A hint in my story?"  
"It’s about Hayase-san."  
"...Her?"

As I muttered in surprise, Louise explained logically.  
"After all, Hayase-san was present when you used your power. I think she might have overheard the conversation with the attackers."

Indeed, Hayase-san knew about my information, and it was highly likely she was a source.  
"No, I thought it was just the attackers leaking it... Alison mentioned that the possibility of an insider was high."

Louise denied this.  
"If they did that, it would be like announcing that they were the culprits, wouldn’t it? If the source of the information was suspected, it would be a problem for them."

While I thought Louise’s opinion was valid, I decided to ask about something that had been bothering me during the attack.  
"By the way, do you know who the attackers were? I thought you might know something."  
"Eh? W-Why do you think that?"

For just a moment, Louise’s gaze wandered.  
"I don’t think you’re one of the attackers. It’s just that you were speaking in a foreign language, so I thought you might know something."

What had Louise and the attackers discussed back then? As I pondered, Louise smiled with a troubled expression.  
"When I get flustered, I tend to slip into my native language... It’s not like I did it on purpose."

I recalled that Louise occasionally spoke in French.  
"That’s right."

As I accepted this, Louise began to explain the situation from that time.  
"I was surprised too. They responded to the words that came out instinctively."  
"What kind of conversation was it?"  
"I don’t remember since it was so sudden, but it felt like they were teasing me."  
"...Could it be that foreign forces are involved?"  
"Who knows? They spoke fluent Japanese too. Besides, there are many who can speak it, especially those like me whose home country is foreign. There’s been an increase in studying abroad and such."

While the possibility of an external intrusion was considered low, it couldn’t be completely ruled out. This only made the profile of the perpetrators more elusive. Louise spoke in a definitive tone, seemingly convinced that Hayase-san was the culprit.  
"To get back on track, you mentioned that Hayase-san brought the female students to observe during the experiment, right? I think she used her ace privileges to obtain confidential information."  
"Why would an ace have such privileges?"

I found it hard to understand. While aces are valued in the military, that doesn’t mean they should have access to classified information. Without the appropriate rank or position, touching on confidential matters isn’t permitted.

Louise averted her gaze slightly as she answered my question.  
"Because the academy is a military-like organization but not a real military. I’ve heard that aces are granted privileges and can access confidential information."

She seemed to be saying that it was an organization close to the military but not an actual military. Since coming to the academy, I had been surprised repeatedly, but I never imagined that aces would be given such disproportionate authority.

Even though she was an ace among the Valkyries, she was still just one combat asset. They shouldn’t have the right to access confidential matters so easily. While I was left speechless, Louise began to speculate about the events in the classroom.  
"Maybe she leaked your information to the girls in Class Five. I’ve heard that Hayase-san has a personal grudge against Gijuu, and she probably can’t stand the experiments you underwent."  
"A personal grudge?"  
"Yeah. There was a massive outbreak of gates ten years ago, right? It seems like there were various issues during that time."

Many people harbored grudges against Gijuu. Especially when recalling the events from ten years ago, it wouldn’t be surprising for someone Hayase-san’s age to have a direct grudge. Louise kept her gaze averted, looking down slightly.  
"It wasn’t direct, but I’ve heard she went through a lot due to the aftermath."

It was indeed a tough time back then. I lost my family during the large-scale outbreak ten years ago. After that, I was sent to an organization’s facility and raised as a soldier.  
"I can understand why Hayase-san might harbor feelings of hatred towards me."  
"Ichinose-kun?"

Louise seemed a bit surprised that I accepted Hayase-san’s feelings. However, even if I understood her feelings, I couldn’t stop the experiments.  
"However, for me, the current project is my very reason for existence. Even if I understand, I cannot stop without orders."

Right now, I was a test pilot for the prototype experimental machine and an experimental subject embedded with Gijuu cells. For my existence in the Prometheus Project, the only goal left for me was to ensure the success of this project.

Louise looked at me intently.  
"Is that okay? I think Hayase-san and the others will try to interfere in various ways from now on."

Worried for me, I shared my past experiences with Louise.  
"I faced severe bullying during my time as an infantryman. I can handle it."

As I declared this, Louise smiled. She clasped her hands behind her back, leaning slightly forward and looking up at me.  
"You’re quite reliable, Ichinose-kun. In that case, I’ll lend you my strength. If anything happens, consult me, okay?"  
"Thank you."

I never expected to hear such words from a younger woman. Still, it was a problem to have the academy's ace taking an interest in me. If Louise’s words were true, it meant Hayase-san had been granted powers that wouldn’t be possible in a normal unit.

Dealing with this from my position would undoubtedly present difficulties.  
"Well then, I’ll return to the development team to explain the details."

As I left the rooftop, Louise waved goodbye.  
"Make sure to come back before the afternoon classes."
